newsitem.title: UK: Rains bring relief for UK crops, more needed.
newsitem.headline: Rains bring relief for UK crops, more needed.

text.p: Rains over the weekend boosted developing cereals crops in the UK's main growing areas, but more is required after a prolonged dry spell, farmers said.

"It has certainly relieved some pressure," one said. Based in Norfolk, he is farming on relatively heavy soil, which absorbs and holds moisture well, he said. Farmers on lighter land may be having more problems.
Between Friday and Sunday, 18 millimetres of rain fell on south-eastern England, the London Weather Centre said. Most of Northern Ireland, England and Wales had rain, a spokesman said.

But the wet weather was not likely to continue for much longer. "It looks like high pressure (giving dry weather) in southern England on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday," a spokesman for the UK Meteorological Office said on Monday. But showers are forecast in most parts of England for Monday.

Although the rain had boosted crops, concern remained that stocks of water were still far too low, posing a threat to future irrigation needs. The Norfolk farmer noted that he had never seen local reservoirs so low, adding, "And it's still only April."
